summary: BUG B (Org add-site shows success, not a false failure) — VERIFIED PASS end-to-end via Playwright on the live preview URL. Logged in as master admin, opened iso-demo-org via org-users-btn (to open the drawer), switched to the Sites tab (org-tab-sites-iso-demo-org), opened the add-site form (org-sites-add-btn-iso-demo-org), entered a unique site name, and submitted (new-site-submit). The POST /api/master-admin/organizations/iso-demo-org/sites returned 200, the success toast 'Site \'QA Test Site <ts>\' added' was captured, the new site row appeared in the panel list, and crucially NO 'Failed to create site' or 'Save failed' toast was shown. The follow-up refresh GET also returned 200, but the code in OrgSitesPanel.js wraps it in its own isolated try/catch so a transient 401 on the refresh can no longer surface as a false 'Failed to create site' error.
critical_code_review_comments: BUG B fix in /app/frontend/src/pages/MasterAdmin/OrgSitesPanel.js (submitNewSite, lines 77-100) is structurally correct AND behaviourally verified: only the POST sits inside the try/catch that can raise notifyApiError('Failed to create site'); the success toast and optimistic setSites([...prev, r.data]) run from the POST response; the follow-up loadSites() refresh is in its own isolated try/catch with an empty catch block — so a transient 401 (or any error) on the refresh GET silently no-ops and cannot surface as a false save error.

Previous testing agent's blocker (clicking the org card row didn't open the drawer) is correctly identified — the chip button data-testid=org-module-chip-{orgId} only renders when the org has module overrides or org-level disabled modules (AdminOrganizations.js lines 866-887 short-circuit return null otherwise). For iso-demo-org (no overrides) the chip is intentionally absent. The working opener is to click org-users-btn-{orgId} (or any tab button that calls toggleExpand) to open the Sheet drawer, then click the data-testid=org-tab-sites-{orgId} tab inside the drawer to switch to the OrgSitesPanel. This is what I did and it works reliably. (Recommendation for E1: documentation note in the prompt mentioning the chip-only-shows-on-overrides condition would prevent future agents from getting stuck.)
Minor: console emits a non-blocking shadcn warning 'Missing Description or aria-describedby={undefined} for DialogContent' on the drawer — accessibility nit, not functional.
seed_data_creation: Two test sites were created on iso-demo-org during retest runs: 'QA Test Site 1782337100' and 'QA Test Site 1782337147'. They can be cleaned up via DELETE on /api/master-admin/organizations/iso-demo-org/sites/{site_id} or by re-running scripts/seed_site_isolation_demo.py.
context_for_next_testing_agent: BUG B is verified PASS. The correct UI path to open OrgSitesPanel for an org that has NO module overrides (e.g., iso-demo-org) is: (1) click org-users-btn-{orgId} to open the right-side Sheet drawer, then (2) click org-tab-sites-{orgId} tab inside the drawer. The org-module-chip-{orgId} opener documented in the prompt only renders if the org has disabled modules or site-level overrides (AdminOrganizations.js:866-887). Observed network: POST /api/master-admin/organizations/iso-demo-org/sites -> 200, followed by GET refresh -> 200. Captured toast: "Site 'QA Test Site <ts>' added". No false 'Failed to create site' / 'Save failed' surfaced.
rca of the issue: Original bug: in OrgSitesPanel.submitNewSite, the POST and the follow-up loadSites() refresh GET were both inside the same try/catch. When the POST succeeded (site persisted) but the immediately-following refresh GET hit a transient 401, the unified catch ran notifyApiError(..., 'Failed to create site'), giving the user a false 'Save failed (401)' message even though the site WAS saved. Fix (verified): keep only the POST inside the try/catch that surfaces 'Failed to create site' + show success + optimistically push r.data into local sites state; wrap the follow-up loadSites() in its own isolated try/catch with a silent catch so refresh errors never surface as save failures. Repro now requires forcing a 401 on the refresh GET only (not on the POST) — even then, the UI now shows success + new row and swallows the refresh error.
